title: Lopud Itinerary 2027: One Day and Two Day Plans
metaDescription: Lopud itinerary for 2027: ferry times, Šunj Beach, Franciscan monastery, Sutvrač fortress, buggy and ferry prices in euros, plus one-day and two-day plans.
content:
## Quick Overview of Lopud

Lopud is a car-free island in the Elaphiti archipelago, about 16 km northwest of Dubrovnik. It has one village, one harbor, a long pedestrian seafront and a sandy beach on the far side of the island at Šunj. The island is small enough that every sight below sits within roughly 2 km of the ferry pier.

## How to Get to Lopud

### Ferry from Dubrovnik

Jadrolinija line 807 is the standard passenger ferry from Dubrovnik's Gruž harbour. Adult fares are €3.40 one way in the off-season and €5.40 in the high season. In 2026 the higher fare ran from 29 May to 27 September, and a similar pattern is likely in 2027. Children aged 3–12 pay about €1.90. The fare is the same in both directions, so a summer return costs €10.80.

The crossing takes about 45 minutes on the passenger ship and up to 1 hour 25 minutes on the car ferry (line 831), which calls at Koločep first. Summer departures from Gruž are several a day on line 807. The last boat back from Lopud usually leaves around 8 pm in summer. Confirm the 2027 timetable on the Jadrolinija website before travel, because times change between seasons.

### Getting around once you arrive

There are no cars on Lopud. Walking covers everything. Electric buggies run between the village and Šunj for about €3 each way.

## One-Day Lopud Itinerary

### 09:00–10:00: Arrive and walk the harbor

Take the earliest ferry possible. Day-trip groups from tour boats arrive by late morning, and the first two hours are the quietest. The seafront promenade runs along the bay, lined with palms, pine trees and a few cafés. Coffee here costs roughly €2–3.

### 10:00–11:30: Franciscan Monastery and the village

The Franciscan Monastery of Our Lady of the Cave (Gospa od Špilice) stands at the entrance to the bay. The cloister dates from 1483. It was strengthened with a high wall in 1516 and a fortress tower in 1592. The complex was abandoned in 1808 and has since been restored. Visitors can usually enter the small church in the courtyard. Entry to the monastery interior is by appointment, so do not count on walking in without notice. The 30 m bell tower and the Venetian artwork are the main draws.

Afterward, walk the village lanes. Lopud has more than 30 churches and chapels, many of them small and ruined, plus a small botanical park.

### 11:30–13:00: Walk to Šunj

The route from the village to Šunj Beach is about 2 km and takes 20–30 minutes each way. It crosses the island's spine, with some stairs and rocky stretches, so wear proper shoes. Above the beach stands the 15th-century Church of Our Lady of Šunj.

### 13:00–16:00: Šunj Beach and lunch

Šunj is one of the few sandy beaches in the Dubrovnik area. The sea stays shallow for many meters, which makes it a good choice for children. The main section has sunbeds and umbrellas for rent (€10–15 for a pair), simple beach bars, toilets and outdoor showers. Shade is limited, so bring a hat or rent an umbrella. Beach prices are high, so carrying water and snacks from the village saves money. Meals at beach restaurants run roughly €12–22.

Water sports such as kayaking and jet skiing are available in season.

### 16:00–19:30: Return and optional fortress climb

Take the buggy or walk back to the village. If there is still light and energy, the hike to the ruined Sutvrač Fortress (built 1563, at the island's highest point) takes about an hour round trip. It is steep and exposed. Go in late afternoon, not at midday. The panorama covers the whole archipelago.

Then catch the evening ferry, or stay for dinner in the village before the last boat.

## Two-Day Lopud Itinerary

Staying one night changes the island. After the last day-trip ferry leaves around 8 pm, the harbor empties and the promenade becomes quiet.

- **Day 1:** Arrive on a mid-morning ferry, check in, swim at the village beach, visit the monastery, and eat dinner on the waterfront.
- **Day 2:** Walk early to Šunj before the day-trippers arrive, then climb Sutvrač in the cooler morning light. Leave on an afternoon ferry.

Hotels start around €60 a night, but rooms are limited in summer. Book early for July and August. Lopud has few places to buy groceries, so plan meals ahead.

## Best Time to Visit Lopud

- **June and September:** Warm sea, fewer crowds, and ferries on the summer schedule.
- **July and August:** Hottest and busiest. Šunj fills by midday.
- **May and October:** Quiet, with fewer ferries and some seasonal restaurants closed.

## Insider Tips for Lopud

- Buy the return ferry ticket at the Gruž ticket office or in advance online during July and August, when queues build up.
- Walk to Šunj on the way there and take the buggy back, when you are tired and sandy.
- The village beach next to the harbor is shallow and free, a fair backup when Šunj is crowded.
- Take cash. Small beach bars and some cafés may not accept cards.
- The ferry from Gruž leaves from the main port, not the Old Town harbor. Allow time to reach it by bus or taxi.

## Is Lopud Worth It? A Straight Opinion

The Sutvrač fortress climb sounds like a good idea at 1 pm in August, and it is not. The ruins are modest, the path has little shade, and the view is the only reward. Do it at sunset or skip it. The better use of midday is Šunj, a long lunch and a swim.

## Lopud Cost Estimate

A day trip from Dubrovnik costs about €45–75 per person. That covers a return ferry (€6.80–10.80), lunch (€12–22), a sunbed (€10–15) and the buggy (€3 each way). Skipping the sunbed and carrying snacks brings it close to €30.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Lopud?
faq.answer: One full day is enough for the village, the monastery, Šunj Beach and lunch. Two days is better if you want to swim, hike to Sutvrač and enjoy the island after the day-trippers leave.

faq.question: How do I get from Dubrovnik to Lopud?
faq.answer: Take the Jadrolinija line 807 passenger ferry from Gruž harbour. It takes about 45–60 minutes and costs €3.40 off-season or €5.40 in summer one way.

faq.question: How far is Šunj Beach from Lopud village?
faq.answer: Šunj Beach is about 2 km from the village. The walk takes 20–30 minutes each way, and a buggy costs about €3 each way.

faq.question: Are there cars on Lopud?
faq.answer: No. The island is car-free, and visitors walk or use electric buggies. This is why the seafront and lanes are calm.

faq.question: Can you visit the Franciscan monastery on Lopud?
faq.answer: The courtyard and small church are usually accessible. The monastery interior is by appointment, so contact the property ahead if you want a full visit.

faq.question: What is the last ferry from Lopud to Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: In summer the last departure is usually around 8 pm. Off-season service is thinner, so confirm the day's timetable with Jadrolinija before relying on a late return.

faq.question: Is Lopud good for families with children?
faq.answer: Yes. The island has no cars, and both the village beach and Šunj have shallow water. Shade at Šunj is limited, so pack sun protection.

quickAnswer: A one-day Lopud itinerary starts with the morning Jadrolinija ferry from Dubrovnik (Gruž), about 45–60 minutes and €3.40–5.40 one way. Spend the morning in the village and Franciscan monastery, walk or ride a buggy to Šunj Beach for lunch and swimming, then take an evening ferry back.
